title: 中国开源AI凭什么火遍全球？乌镇峰会揭秘：调用量连续 27 周超越美国，成海外企业和开发者的香饽饽
content:
At the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit held in Wuzhen, Zhejiang, the topic of the AI open-source ecosystem became the focus of everyone’s attention. In recent years, China’s large AI models have continued to win fans around the world thanks to continuous technological iteration, high performance, and strong cost-effectiveness, showing powerful international competitiveness.
Global data confirms: Chinese large models lead in usage, with DeepSeek at the top
The popularity of Chinese large AI models is backed by detailed data. According to statistics from OpenRouter, a global AI model aggregation platform, during the week from October 26 to November 1, the token usage of Chinese large models exceeded that of the United States for 27 consecutive weeks. At the same time, among the top five models by total weekly token usage globally, Chinese large AI models took four spots, with DeepSeek ranking first.
Gao Xi, a research engineer at DeepSeek, noted that from early basic chat and translation functions to today’s deep logical reasoning and ability to truly solve users’ real-life problems, Chinese large AI models have developed at an unimaginable pace, maintaining a rhythm of significant technological innovation and breakthroughs almost every year.
International experts give thumbs up: Silicon Valley and European SMEs become loyal users
In terms of international applications, Chinese open-source models have also gained broad recognition. John Hoffman, Chairman of the GSMA, said that some of China’s large language models and the small language models under development have made tremendous progress, and the vast majority are built on open-source platforms.
Bernd Holznagel, a professor at the University of Münster in Germany and a hands-on user of DeepSeek, observed that many companies in Silicon Valley in the United States and nearly half of small and medium-sized enterprises in Germany now widely use Chinese open-source large AI models in their daily work.
Joseph Tsai, co-founder and chairman of Alibaba Group, pointed out that Chinese open-source models have strong overall performance and high inference efficiency, giving them very strong competitiveness globally. Over the past year, global AI application scenarios have been rapidly expanding into fields such as industrial manufacturing, healthcare, public services, corporate office work, and technology R&D. Chinese tech companies’ continued efforts to increase open-source and ecosystem openness have kept key indicators such as open-source model downloads and the number of derivative models in the lead.
Breaking down “small yards with high fences”: open-source ecosystems help close the digital divide
Experts at the event generally agreed that if AI technology is locked tightly behind “small yards with high fences,” sparks of innovation will find it hard to spread, ultimately hindering the overall progress of global technology. The open and shared “open-source” trend, however, is opening up broader imaginative space for future AI innovation.
Tsai said that open source can greatly reduce R&D costs for SMEs, especially enabling developers in emerging economies to quickly create AI applications that meet their countries’ needs based on open-source models. For example, a nonprofit organization in Uganda developed a local language model based on the Qwen model. It now covers 68 African languages, helping more local people break through language barriers and successfully access and use advanced AI technology.
Liu Dayiheng, head of the Qwen large language model project at Alibaba’s ATH business group, said bluntly that without open source, the core technology of large AI models might remain monopolized by a small number of people and companies for a long time. Through open source, scholars and students lacking resources can acquire cutting-edge knowledge and participate in technological innovation at extremely low cost; and minority languages, special vertical applications, or specific hardware compatibility issues that big tech companies may not have the time to address can also be effectively solved with the collective wisdom of open-source communities. In addition, the high cost-effectiveness of open-source models themselves also plays a positive role in preventing price monopolies in the market.

report.summary: 中国开源大模型调用量连续27周超美，全球加速采用。
report.background: 在2026年乌镇世界互联网大会上，AI开源生态成为焦点。近年中国大模型依靠持续迭代、高性能和高性价比加速走向全球。OpenRouter统计显示，2026年10月26日至11月1日当周，中国大模型token调用量已连续27周超过美国；全球周调用量前五中中国模型占四席，DeepSeek居首。开源正成为中美AI竞争和全球普及的关键变量。
key_points: 调用量是硬指标：OpenRouter数据显示中国大模型连续27周token使用量超美国，说明海外开发者和企业已在实际业务中规模化采用。
头部效应明显：全球周调用量前五名中，中国大模型占四席，DeepSeek排名第一，Qwen等模型形成开源阵营合力。
海外中小企业成主力：硅谷公司和近半数德国中小企业已在日常工作中使用中国开源模型，原因包括性能、推理效率和成本优势。
开源降低创新门槛：乌干达机构基于Qwen开发覆盖68种非洲语言的本土模型，显示开源能帮助新兴市场快速做本地化AI应用。
开源打破技术垄断：专家认为开放共享可避免核心技术被少数公司长期垄断，也能防止价格垄断并补齐小语种、垂直场景和硬件兼容需求。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，中国开源模型的规模化调用正在改变“闭源领先”的叙事，竞争重心转向性能、成本和生态开放度。对开发者来说，可直接基于DeepSeek、Qwen等权重做微调、本地部署和垂直应用，试错成本显著降低。对普通用户，更多低价甚至免费的AI应用将进入办公、医疗、公共服务和小语种场景，数字鸿沟有望缩小，但也需关注数据安全、许可合规和模型治理。
report.tools: 想跟进可关注DeepSeek、Qwen系列开源模型，用OpenRouter观察调用趋势和模型对比；在Hugging Face或ModelScope获取权重，结合Ollama、vLLM做本地部署与推理优化，并留意开源许可证和多语言微调工具。
